analysis.title: King dollar tightens its grip
key_insights: The US dollar rose against all G10 currencies on Monday 16 Nov. Natixis cites hotter-than-expected October US inflation and hawkish Fed comments, which pushed markets to price a more restrictive Fed.
Markets now price around 2.5 Fed rate hikes by March 2027. Natixis's own research highlights also say US inflation prints 'cement' a December hike.

EUR/USD fell below 1.10 after reaching 1.1250 the prior week. Hawkish ECB comments gave the euro little support. Natixis says the dollar's advance could continue for a few more weeks if risk aversion stays elevated, potentially taking EUR/USD to 1.0950.
DXY rose to 103.5, its highest level since April 2025. One-month EUR/USD implied volatility rose to 6.5%.
Geopolitical risks that keep oil and gas prices at current levels could feed inflation and keep central bank policy rates higher for longer.

Uncertainty around Nvidia ahead of its earnings on 17 Nov added to market jitters and indirectly supported the dollar as a safe haven. A US tech sell-off preceded the results and Anthropic's IPO scheduled for Wednesday 18 Nov.
Equities fell. In Europe the SXXE lost 1.6% and ASML 2.4%, with the V2X at 18.3. In the US the SPX fell 1.2% and the Nasdaq 1.7%. Defensive sectors rose in Europe.
The 10Y UST yield approached 5.15% by the European close. The 10Y Bund stayed within its 3.35-3.40% range and curves steepened slightly.

The 10Y OAT-Bund spread widened by more than 2 bps to above 155 bps as equities declined. Natixis's Fast Money positioning index was neutral on the spread at the end of the prior week, so the equity sell-off may have prompted new short positions in French debt.
Credit indices widened. iTraxx Main rose 1bp and X-Over 3.5bp, CDX IG 0.7bp. Oracle CDS widened 6bp and SpaceX CDS 3bp. Nvidia CDS widened 1bp ahead of results and amid recent news about its CEO.
Euro corporate primary: 13 issues totalled EUR 8.9bn, with Merck the largest at EUR 3.7bn. Average new issue premium was about 22bp and subscription rates ranged from 2.3x to 5.2x.

Data: US Empire State Manufacturing fell to 7.8 in November from 25.5. Canada October CPI rose 0.2% m/m vs 0.3% expected and core slowed to 1.8% y/y. Euro area September industrial production rose 0.2% m/m. UK unemployment fell to 4.6%.

UniCredit has Fed approval and unconditional EU approval for its takeover of Commerzbank, with Polish approval the remaining hurdle. Natixis views the deal as credit positive for both and notes execution, integration and political risks remain.

Credit rating actions: Moody's cut Volvo Cars to Ba2 from Ba1 (negative outlook, FCF only modestly positive in 2028) and Virgin Media O2 to B2 from B1. Eutelsat is offering EUR 400mn of 2032 notes with initial price talk around 8.5%, roughly 180bp wider than its secondary curve.
earnings_insights: Nvidia's earnings were due on 17 Nov, with the results not yet reported at the time of writing. Telefonica Q3-26: strong cash generation is driving deleveraging, supported by resilient growth in Spain and Brazil, while weaker earnings in Germany, VMO2 challenges and Brazil currency risk complicate the plan.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The hotter print contributed to dollar strength and pricing of a more restrictive Fed.

macro_indicators.indicator: Fed rate hikes priced by March 2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: Market-implied tightening supports the dollar against the euro.
A sharp slowdown in New York-area manufacturing activity.
Softer than expected. Core inflation excluding food and energy slowed to 1.8% y/y from a revised 2.0%.
Possible downside level if risk aversion stays elevated.

risk_factors: Prolonged risk aversion around Nvidia's results and the Anthropic IPO could extend dollar strength.
Oil and gas prices staying elevated on geopolitical risk could lift inflation and keep policy rates higher for longer.
UniCredit's Commerzbank takeover still faces Polish regulatory approval, plus execution, integration and political risks.
Volvo Cars faces weak profitability, negative FCF, rising debt, US tariffs and a delayed EX60 launch.
vol_and_positioning: One-month EUR/USD implied volatility rose to 6.5% as the pair tested 1.10.
V2X closed at 18.3. VIX futures were at 22.3, up 3.4 points on the day.
Natixis's Fast Money positioning index showed a neutral position on the OAT-Bund spread at the end of the prior week, and the equity sell-off may have prompted new shorts.
geopolitical: Geopolitical risks that keep oil and gas prices at current levels are weighing on EUR/USD and could keep inflation high and central banks on hold at higher rates.
